Abdominal Wall Anatomy

Abdominal wall

Abdominal wall connects the rib cage superiorly with the pelvis inferiorly

Abdominal wall is composed of muscle, bone and fascia

it functions as a protective barrier enclosing the GIT and urogenital organs but it also has a role in mobility (flexion, extension, rotation)

Anterolaterally from superficial to deep

Skin

Subcutaneous tissue

Fascia

Fatty superficial fascia (Camper’s fascia)

Deep fibrous fascia (Scarpa’s fascia)

Muscles

External oblique

Internal oblique

Rectus abdominis

Transversus abdominus

Transversalis fascia

Fat

Parietal peritoneum

Anterolaterally

Anterolateral muscles extend from ribs to pelvis and they are supplied by thoracoabdominal nerves T7-T11, subcostal nerve T12, iliohypogastric, lateral cutaneous and ilioinguinal nerve

Posteriorly

Skin

Subcutaneous tissue

Spine

Muscles

Quadratus lumborum (most superficial) originates from iliac crest and insert into transverse processes of L1-L4 and inferior border of 12th rib and it is supplied by anterior rami of T12- L4 nerves, it work as extensor and lateral flexor of the spinal column

Psoas major (deeper to quadratus lumborum): originates from the transverse process of T12-L5 and attaches to lesser trochanter of the femur, it is supplied by anterior rami of L1-L3 nerves , it work as a thigh flexor and a lateral flexor of spinal column

Psoas minor (deeper to psoas major): originates from vertebral bodies T12- L1 and attaches to superior ramus of pubic bone, supplied by anterior rami of the L1 nerve and work as flexor for the vertebral column

Iliacus: originates from surface of iliac fossa and anterior inferior iliac spine, and insert to lesser trochanter of the femur, supplied by femoral nerve L2-L4 and work as a flexor and lateral rotator for the femur bone

Posterior aspect of the diaphragm

Fascia

Thoracolumbar fascia: most superficial (more superficial than quadratus lumborum)

Psoas fascia: covers psoas and it is deeper than psoas muscles

So the two fascias enclose the posterior abdominal muscles

Abdominal pressure

Roof of the abdomen is formed by the diaphragm which separates thoracic cavity above from the abdominal cavity below

Thoracic cavity has negative pressure while abdominal cavity has positive pressure

Weakness of diaphragm can lead to bowel herniating to thoracic cavity
